Q: YouTube Error 153: Video Player Configuration Error when embedding YouTube videos A:

This is worked for me:

val iFrameHtmlData = """<iframe width="100%" height="100%" src="$iframeUrl" frameborder="0" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>""".trimIndent()

Q: Operation is not allowed - firebase phone verification code A:

The following error:

This operation is not allowed. This may be due to the given sign-in provider being disabled of this Firebase project.

Tells you exactly what the problem is. You need to enable the Phone Sign-in method inside the Authentication section of your project inside the Firebase Console.

But please make sure, the Phone Authentication is Enabled in the correct Firebase Project. So verify the project_id that exists inside the google-services.json to match with the one that exists in the Firebase Console.

Aside from that, make sure you have enabled billing Phone Authentication requires the billing to be enabled in your project.

Q: Related to NextJs Search Engine Optimization A:

Difference between pages/ and app/ folder in Next.js

Both folders are used for routing in Next.js, but they belong to different routing systems and have different capabilities.

  • pages/ folder (Pages Router)

    This is the original routing system used in Next.js for many years.

    • Each file automatically becomes a route
      (pages/index.js → /, pages/blog/[id].js → /blog/1)

    • Data fetching is handled using special functions like:

      • getStaticProps

      • getServerSideProps

      • getStaticPaths

    • Components are rendered on the client by default

    • Layouts are usually handled using _app.js and _document.js

    • It is stable, well-documented, and still fully supported

    This approach works well for small to medium apps and existing projects that were built before Next.js 13.

  • app/ folder (App Router – Next.js 13+)

    The app/ folder is the newer routing system, introduced in Next.js 13.

    • Routing is folder-based, with page.js defining routes

    • Shared layouts are handled using layout.js

    • Uses React Server Components by default, which improves performance

    • Data fetching is done directly inside components using fetch()

    • Supports advanced features like:

      • Nested layouts

      • Streaming and Suspense

      • Built-in metadata handling for SEO

    This approach is better suited for new applications and larger, more complex projects.

In short:
Use pages/ for existing or simple projects, and app/ for new projects where you want modern features and better performance.
